reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Ω be a measurable space, let μ be a measure on Ω, and let B assign to each nonnegative real time a real-valued random variable on Ω. Assume IsPreBrownianReal B μ, and fix T ∈ ℝ≥0. At level ℓ ∈ ℕ, partition the interval from 0 to T into 2^ℓ equal cells, using the regular grid with mesh T / 2^ℓ, and form the quadratic-variation error by summing, over all cells, each squared increment of B minus that cell's length. Then the μ-integral of the square of this full error converges to 0 as ℓ tends to infinity: lim_{ℓ→∞} ∫ ω, (quadraticVariationError B (regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T ℓ) (2^ℓ)) ω)² ∂μ = 0.
objects: A measurable sample space Ω; a measure μ on Ω; a real-valued process B indexed by nonnegative real times; a fixed terminal time T; a natural-number refinement level ℓ; the dyadic mesh T / 2^ℓ; the regular grid with 2^ℓ cells and 2^ℓ + 1 points; and the quadratic-variation error on that grid.
domains: T and every grid time lie in ℝ≥0. The refinement level ℓ lies in ℕ. B maps nonnegative times to real-valued random variables on Ω. The quadratic-variation error is real-valued on Ω, its square is integrated over Ω with respect to μ, and the resulting level-indexed quantity is real-valued.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over the ambient process B and measure μ, conditional on hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ, and universally quantified over T : ℝ≥0. The convergence variable level is implicitly universally ranged over ℕ by the function tending along atTop.
assumptions: The sample space is measurable and μ is a measure. The condition IsPreBrownianReal B μ provides centered Gaussian increments with variance equal to elapsed time and independence on ordered deterministic grids. No positivity assumption on T is required, so T = 0 is included. The grids are deterministic regular dyadic grids.
conclusion: As the natural-number level tends to infinity, the μ-integral of the squared quadratic-variation error on the regular grid with mesh dyadicMesh T level and 2^level cells tends to zero. Equivalently, this quadratic-variation error converges to zero in mean square along the dyadic refinements of [0,T].
scopes: The same level controls both the mesh denominator 2^level and the number 2^level of grid cells. The square inside the integral applies to the entire finite-sum quadratic-variation error. The integral is over ω with respect to μ. Tendsto applies to the complete real-valued sequence of these integrals, with source filter atTop and target neighborhood filter nhds 0.
constant_dependencies: The terminal limit 0 and dyadic base 2 are universal constants. The sequence depends on B, μ, and T, while its level-dependent grid has 2^level cells of common length T / 2^level. The theorem asserts convergence only and introduces no level-dependent rate or additional constant.
